title: Docs + runbooks for offline bundle signature verification (Support/SE readiness)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Ensure Support + Solutions Engineering have customer-ready troubleshooting materials for air-gapped installs *before pilot*. This ticket is the engineering-owned packaging of runbooks + docs pointers, aligned to the installer’s verification behavior (fail-closed) and error taxonomy.

Background
We’re introducing signed offline bundles for Redwood Private installs in air-gapped environments. The installer preflight verifies:
- bundle manifest integrity (hashes)
- signature validity (trusted key, valid time window)
- downgrade protection (signed version metadata + local state)
- SBOM pointer/hash presence (where applicable)

Support/SE need:
- a single “how to verify + interpret errors” guide
- a day-2 ops runbook for failures with log paths + collection steps
- customer-safe remediation steps that don’t weaken security posture
- clear break-glass instructions + required approvals/logging

Deliverables (must land before pilot kickoff)
1) Internal Support/SE guide (Confluence): step-by-step air-gapped install + verification
   - Preflight verification commands and expected output
   - Common failure modes and what to collect
   - When to escalate to Release Eng vs Security Eng

2) Day-2 runbook (Confluence): verification failures
   - Error code taxonomy mapping to causes/remediations
   - Log locations (installer logs + audit events), support bundle notes
   - Offline transport integrity checks (zip/tar pitfalls)

3) FAQ + common errors (Docs site)
   - Customer-facing explanation of signature verification and trust store updates
   - “Unknown key after rotation” and “time skew” guidance

4) Break-glass path documentation (internal + customer-facing stance)
   - How to use override flag (if enabled) and what it records
   - Approval path and mandatory post-incident remediation

Non-goals
- Writing the canonical crypto standard (covered by architecture standard + ADR)
- Changing installer behavior (tracked in ENG-4823/4824 and related PRs)

Audience
- Solutions Engineering (pilots + onboarding)
- Support (P1/P0 install blockers)
- Customer platform ops/security teams (via customer-facing docs)

Source-of-truth pointers (to link/align with)
- Confluence: Offline signing + verification design
- Confluence: Threat model for offline bundle signing
- Confluence: Break-glass exception process
- GitHub PRs: verification error messaging, inspect command, support bundle metadata

Acceptance criteria
- Support readiness review completed with Dev Patel + Owen Phillips (sign-off in comments)
- SE readiness review completed with Fatima Noor + Colin O’Donnell (sign-off in comments)
- Docs include the final CLI names/flags for:
  - inspect/verify bundle
  - preflight verification
  - break-glass override (if applicable)
- Runbook includes:
  - at least 8 “known issues” entries (hash mismatch, unknown key, expired/not-yet-valid, manifest parse/canonicalization mismatch, downgrade blocked, missing SBOM hash, tampered artifact, unsupported installer/bundle version)
  - exact log paths + how to generate support bundle
  - escalation matrix + what artifacts to attach
- Links are added to pilot execution checklist (PM-907) and GA checklist (PM-894)

Implementation notes
- Engineering owns correctness of commands/output and log locations.
- Docs team owns final wording/IA; engineering provides structured content + screenshots from staging.
- Ensure alignment with:
  - downgrade prevention copy (avoid implying customers can bypass without approval)
  - key rotation story (trust store updates in air-gapped env)
  - audit event schema/redaction (don’t suggest collecting secrets)

Open questions (resolved in comments)
- Final names for CLI subcommands and flags (inspect/verify vs preflight)
- Whether we document time override for diagnostics and how we gate it
- What we call the trust store file and how customers update it offline
